title: YouTube content research agent with transcript analysis
metaTitle: YouTube content research agent in n8n | Pixel2Tech
metaDescription: An n8n agent that scrapes YouTube videos and transcripts with Apify, then uses OpenAI to pull key concepts, themes and content angles into Google Sheets.
summary: An n8n workflow that collects YouTube videos on a topic, pulls their transcripts and uses AI to extract key concepts, recurring themes and unique angles into a research sheet.
overview: We built this agent for a content team that plans videos by studying what already performs on YouTube. A team member submits a search through a form. The workflow uses Apify to find videos and fetch their transcripts, then an OpenAI agent with a structured output parser breaks each transcript down into key concepts, recurring themes and unique angles and writes one row per video to Google Sheets.
challenge: Researching a topic on YouTube means watching hours of video and taking notes by hand. The notes end up scattered, and it is hard to compare what different creators cover or where the gaps are.
approach: An n8n form collects the search input. An HTTP request runs an Apify YouTube scraper to find matching videos, and a second Apify actor extracts each transcript. A code step cleans and combines the data. An AI agent on an OpenAI chat model analyzes each transcript, and a structured output parser makes sure the result always has the same fields. A final code step formats the row, and the workflow appends the title, link, transcript, key concepts, recurring themes, unique angles and view count to Google Sheets.
outcome: The team now gets a structured research sheet for any topic in one run, with each video's ideas and angles side by side, ready for planning new content.

whyItMatters: Seeing what other videos cover, and what they miss, is the fastest way to find a fresh angle, and this workflow turns hours of viewing into a sheet you can scan.

faqs.q: Can it analyze a specific channel or playlist?
faqs.a: Yes. The Apify input can target a channel, a playlist or a list of video links instead of a keyword search.
